title: Target Sum
description:
Place exactly one plus or minus sign in front of every number in nums, then add the signed numbers. Return how many assignments produce target. Assignments are distinguished by position: choosing a plus for the first of two equal numbers differs from choosing a plus for the second.

Even zero has two sign choices, +0 and -0, and those choices count as different assignments. The empty list has one assignment (the empty sum, zero). Count assignments rather than distinct expressions after simplification.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,1,1,1,1], target = 3
Output: 5

Choose one of the five ones to be negative.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1], target = 1
Output: 1

The plus sign on the only 1 yields the target.

Example 3:

Input: nums = [], target = 0
Output: 1

The empty sum is zero in exactly one way.

Constraints:

  • 0 <= nums.length <= 20
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 100
  • -2000 <= target <= 2000

exampleTestCases.explanation: Choose one of the five ones to be negative.
The plus sign on the only 1 yields the target.
The empty sum is zero in exactly one way.
